Three days in Hong Kong: Central heritage and the Peak skyline on arrival day, a museum day in West Kowloon that stays indoors for the typhoon, and a light last morning of temple, harbour promenade and the Star Ferry. The plan uses the Mong Kok Cordis for both nights and comes in under your HKD 9,000 budget.

Two days that split Hong Kong into its two sides: Day 1 covers Kowloon with a temple, the Palace Museum, a night market and the harbour light show. Day 2 pairs West Kowloon's M+ with a Star Ferry crossing and Central's heritage streets. It stays well under budget and avoids the closed Peak Tram.

It ends with a temple, dim sum and M+ before you head home. Stops are grouped by area to keep transfers short, and the total stays within your HKD 6,000 budget.

A relaxed two-day Hong Kong break with Central's heritage lanes and a Peak sunset on day one, then West Kowloon's Palace Museum, a temple visit and a harbour ferry ride on day two. It is based at Ovolo Central, so you are close to most stops, and the whole trip stays under 5,000 HKD for two.

Day 1 (2027-06-01): Mak's Noodle, Tai Kwun, Man Mo Temple, Victoria Peak.

A compact two-day Hong Kong stay. Day one is an easy afternoon and evening on Hong Kong Island: heritage in Central, then the skyline from Victoria Peak. Day two covers a Kowloon temple, a museum and dim sum, and finishes early so you can get to the airport comfortably. It stays well within the HKD 10,000 budget for three people.

A compact two-night-free, two-day Hong Kong trip for six. Day 1 starts in the afternoon and stays in the Tsim Sha Tsui, Yau Ma Tei and Jordan area, with a harbour crossing, the night market and the 20:00 skyline light show. Day 2 pairs Wong Tai Sin Temple with the Tian Tan Buddha on Lantau, with an early dim sum lunch in between and no MTR.

Day 1 (2027-10-15): Star Ferry, Temple Street Night Mark

Two days that cover Hong Kong's big views and its heritage. Monday is an afternoon of Chinese art in West Kowloon, a Star Ferry crossing and a night-time Peak skyline. Tuesday is a Central morning of temples and heritage, wonton noodles, then M+ before you head home. Both days stay compact and mostly indoors or on short hops, and the total comes in well under your HKD 5,000 budget.

A compact two-day Hong Kong trip. The first afternoon, under the Signal No. 8 forecast, stays indoors in two West Kowloon museums. The second day, with only a chance of showers, covers the harbour ferry, Sheung Wan and Central heritage sites, and the skyline from Victoria Peak. A TST hotel near the first day's museums keeps the total well inside the 5,000 HKD budget.

Four relaxed-to-balanced days in Kyoto that start with an easy Gion evening on arrival. They cover Fushimi Inari, the eastern temples, Arashiyama and the Golden and Silver Pavilions, then finish with a short morning at Nijo Castle and Nishiki Market before you leave. Stops are grouped by district to keep transit short, and the total comes to roughly ¥153,000, well inside the ¥400,000 budget.

Five days in Tokyo that pair classic sights (Senso-ji, Tokyo Tower, Skytree, Meiji Jingu) with a teamLab and Ghibli day and a slower Shinjuku and Aoyama day. The plan assumes you land on the evening of the 3rd, so day one is a light night-view loop. You stay in central Ginza, and the total comes in well under the ¥600,000 budget.

Day 1 (2027-05-03): Tokyo Tower, Afuri Ebisu, Shibuya Crossing.

A three-day Osaka trip that arrives in the afternoon for Shinsekai and the neon of Dotonbori, spends the middle day on the castle, the aquarium and a sunset view over Umeda, and ends with a gentle shrine-and-market morning before departure. Every meal is at a vegan kitchen to keep the trip vegetarian, and the total stays well inside the 250,000 JPY budget.

A two-day Tokyo trip with the Ghibli Museum, Senso-ji and a few classic Tokyo sights. Day 1 is an afternoon-and-evening loop from Asakusa to Shibuya, and Day 2 is a relaxed morning at the Ghibli Museum followed by lunch and a shrine walk. The total comes to roughly ¥118,000 against the ¥200,000 budget.

Day 1 (2027-09-18): Senso-ji, Tokyo Skytree, Afuri Ebisu, Shibuya Crossing.

Day 2 (2027-09-19)

A compact two-day Osaka trip built around Osaka Castle on arrival day, followed by the neon of Dotonbori after dark. Day 2 is a lighter morning of a shrine and the retro Shinsekai district, leaving room for the journey home. Every meal is at a fully vegetarian kitchen, and the plan stays well under budget.

Day 1 (2027-11-20): Osaka Castle, Kuromon Market, Dotonbori, Green Earth.

Three days in Kyoto: a light arrival afternoon in central Kyoto, a full day in the eastern temple and geisha districts built around Kiyomizu-dera, and an early start at Arashiyama and Fushimi Inari before you head home. A station-area hotel keeps the trip well inside the ¥300,000 budget for four.

Day 1 (2027-10-02): Nijo Castle, Nishiki Market, Nishiki Warai.

Three days in New York over Christmas week. You get a sunset view and the lights on arrival, a full morning at the Met on Christmas Eve, and a relaxed last day on the High Line and at MoMA. Stops are grouped by neighbourhood, and the day-by-day plan comes in well under your budget.
